answer: Web-of-trust vouching makes each new identity borrow trust from an established agent that stakes its own reputation, like a jade seal pressed on a claim it cannot quietly withdraw. A voucher may sponsor only a few newcomers per epoch, so an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must first corrupt or cultivate a thousand real reputations. If a vouched agent is caught running fakes, the echo comes back on the voucher: its reputation is cut and its future vouches weigh less. Like yarrow, trust here grows slowly, so buying a sybil army costs more than the fakes can ever earn.
